memory.content: JavaScript URLSearchParams API는 URL 쿼리 문자열을 파싱하고 조작하는 인터페이스입니다. new URL(location.href).searchParams.get('keyword')로 쿼리 파라미터를 추출할 수 있습니다.
HTML form에서 같은 name을 가진 여러 checkbox를 사용하면 선택된 값들이 배열로 서버에 전송됩니다. Spring에서는 @RequestParam List<String>으로 받을 수 있습니다.
Spring MVC는 form 데이터를 자동으로 객체에 바인딩합니다. checkbox의 name attribute가 컨트롤러 파라미터 이름과 일치하면 자동으로 매핑됩니다.
HTML table의 <td> 요소 안에 input checkbox를 배치할 수 있습니다. 각 checkbox의 value는 원래 <td>의 id를 사용하여 데이터를 식별합니다.
HTML <label> 요소는 checkbox와 연결하여 사용성을 높입니다. <label for='id'>나 checkbox를 <label> 안에 감싸는 방식으로 연결할 수 있습니다.
한글 콘텐츠를 다룰 때는 UTF-8 인코딩을 명시하고, Spring에서는 CharacterEncodingFilter를 설정하여 한글 깨짐을 방지합니다.

skills.name: url-param-extraction
skills.description: Extract query parameters from URL using URLSearchParams
skills.content:
# URL param extraction

## Purpose
Extract query parameters from the current page URL using the URLSearchParams API.

## Use when
- A page or script needs a named query parameter from location.href.

## Do not use when
- Parsing path segments or hash fragments; server-side request parameters.

## Inputs
- The current location.href and the parameter name to read.

## Procedure
1. Create a URL object from location.href so the query string is parsed, for example `new URL(location.href)`.
2. Access the searchParams property on that URL object.
3. Call `.get('paramName')` to retrieve the named value (for example keyword).
4. Handle a null return when the parameter is absent: skip the dependent action or apply the page's empty-state behavior instead of assuming a string.

## Verification
- Present parameters return the expected string; missing parameters are treated as null rather than throwing.

## Constraints
- Do not invent extra query keys; only read names the page already uses.

skills.name: checkbox-form-array
skills.description: Create multiple checkboxes that submit as an array
skills.content:
# Checkbox form array

## Purpose
Create multiple checkboxes that submit as an array of checked values.

## Use when
- A form must send several related options (for example allergy types) as one named collection.

## Do not use when
- A single boolean checkbox; radio groups that allow only one choice.

## Inputs
- The option list and a shared form field name.

## Procedure
1. Add checkboxes that share the same name attribute so the browser groups them.
2. Set a unique value on each checkbox so selected options remain distinguishable.
3. Use meaningful IDs from the data (for example allergy types) for both identification and values.
4. Submit the form so the server receives an array of the checked values only.

## Verification
- Checking several boxes posts those values as an array; checking none posts no selected values.

## Constraints
- Do not give each checkbox a different name if they must arrive as one array.

skills.name: table-to-checkbox-conversion
skills.description: Convert table cells with IDs to checkbox inputs
skills.content:
# Table to checkbox conversion

## Purpose
Convert table cells that currently store an id on the td into checkbox inputs.

## Use when
- A table of options needs to become a multi-select form.

## Do not use when
- Cells already contain inputs; converting a layout table unrelated to selection.

## Inputs
- Table markup whose td elements carry identifying ids.

## Procedure
1. Identify the repeating pattern: a table cell of the form `<td id='value'>`.
2. Replace each matching cell with `<td><input type='checkbox' name='commonName' value='id'>`, using the original td id as the checkbox value.
3. Keep the same name attribute across all converted checkboxes so they submit as one array.
4. Preserve unique ids as checkbox values; do not collapse distinct rows into a single value.

## Verification
- Every converted cell is a checkbox; original ids survive as values; names are consistent.

## Constraints
- Do not drop unique identifiers during the bulk replacement.

skills.name: spring-checkbox-binding
skills.description: Bind checkbox array data in Spring controller
skills.content:
# Spring checkbox binding

## Purpose
Bind a checkbox array from the form into a Spring MVC controller parameter.

## Use when
- The controller must receive multiple checkbox values posted under one name.

## Do not use when
- Binding a single scalar field or a full command object that already maps the checkboxes.

## Inputs
- The checkbox name attribute and the controller handler signature.

## Procedure
1. Annotate the handler argument with `@RequestParam`.
2. Declare the parameter as `List<String>` or `String[]` so multiple posted values bind as a collection.
3. Match the parameter name to the checkbox name attribute so Spring maps the posted fields.
4. Handle the case when no checkboxes are selected: treat the result as an empty list rather than a null crash.

## Verification
- Selected boxes arrive as a list of their values; none selected yields an empty list.

## Constraints
- Do not require a dummy hidden field unless the existing form already uses one.

skills.name: label-checkbox-pairing
skills.description: Add labels to checkboxes for better UX
skills.content:
# Label checkbox pairing

## Purpose
Associate visible labels with checkboxes so the control is usable and clickable.

## Use when
- Checkboxes are added or converted and need accessible labels.

## Do not use when
- Non-checkbox inputs that already have a different labeling pattern.

## Inputs
- The checkbox markup and the descriptive text for each option.

## Procedure
1. Add a `<label>` element after or around each checkbox.
2. Connect the label with a `for` attribute matching the checkbox id, or wrap the checkbox inside the label.
3. Put descriptive text in the label so the option meaning is visible.
4. Style labels for better clickability without breaking the for/id pairing.

## Verification
- Clicking the label toggles the matching checkbox; every checkbox has descriptive text.

## Constraints
- Do not leave unlabeled checkboxes in the converted table.

skills.name: bulk-html-modification
skills.description: Perform bulk find-and-replace on HTML structure
skills.content:
# Bulk HTML modification

## Purpose
Perform a bulk find-and-replace on repeating HTML structure while keeping unique values.

## Use when
- The same markup pattern must change in many places (for example td-to-checkbox conversion).

## Do not use when
- A one-off edit of a single element.

## Inputs
- The source HTML and the repeating pattern to replace.

## Procedure
1. Identify the exact pattern to replace, including which parts are unique (ids, values).
2. Use regex or the editor find-replace across all occurrences of that pattern.
3. Preserve unique values (IDs) in the replacement so each instance stays distinct.
4. Verify every instance was updated: scan remaining old-pattern matches and spot-check rendered markup.

## Verification
- No leftover old pattern remains; unique ids still differ per instance.

## Constraints
- Do not apply a global replace that overwrites unique identifiers.
